slot.why: One style sheet drives every picture Muse Image draws for the game (sprites, backdrop, portraits, scene pictures), so they all match: palette, line, lighting and framing.
slot.extrapolate_from: an art-style word in the request (pixel art, 8-bit, retro RPG, watercolor, Ghibli, LEGO, claymation, anime, 80s anime, comic, low poly, papercraft, neon, crayon), else the franchise's own look
slot.ask_when: the request names no art style and the game is art-heavy (the plan has art: "image": a story with characters, or three or more sprite roles); otherwise Muse picks one and says so in the anatomy ("I'm drawing it as bold cartoon art")
slot.notes: The planner replaces the choices with 3-4 styles that fit the theme, and the app adds Other (free text). Examples: Star Wars escape -> 80s anime, comic book, pixel art; medieval peasant -> illuminated storybook, claymation, pixel art; Labubu blind box -> soft vinyl toy, kawaii cartoon, claymation; brainrot runner -> bold cartoon, 3D cartoon, pixel art. The answer goes to the image art step as `style` (authoring/expander/image-art.mjs STYLE_PRESETS, or free text). It counts toward the 2-question limit, so ask it only when nothing more important is open.

notes: A cross-family slot. It lives outside the per-family files (checklists/*.json, which allow at most 6 slots each and are loaded one family per file), so the planner adds it to the retrieved checklist when the plan sets art: "image". adventure_rpg and mystery_narrative carry it directly as well.
